## My Thinking

I farm about 12 mu here in Quzhou. My father farmed it before me. Everyone around here does wheat and corn — winter wheat in fall, summer corn right after. Same rotation, every year. The soil knows it. I know it. It makes sense.

Spring wheat doesn't work well here — winters are cold enough that winter wheat gives a better yield. And after wheat harvest in June, there's still enough season left to get a full corn crop in before October. Two harvests a year off the same land — that's what keeps this family fed and with some cash.

For wheat, I use Jimai 22 — it's an improved variety the seed shop in Quzhou town stocks, good yield, decent resistance to rust. I don't bother with hybrid wheat, the price isn't worth it. I plough before sowing, apply compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress with urea at jointing. Spring in Hebei is dry, so I have to irrigate — four times is what I usually do: once before sowing to settle the soil, once in winter to protect roots from frost heave, once at jointing, once when heading. Skip one of those and yields drop noticeably. I spray herbicide in early spring and keep an eye on aphids and powdery mildew before harvest.

For summer corn, I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 mostly, sometimes whatever the co-op has at a better price. I direct-seed it right into the wheat stubble within a day or two of harvest, no time to waste. Summer rains usually handle most of the water — one irrigation if August turns dry. Herbicide early, one spray for corn borer mid-season.

I'll keep a small patch near the house for garlic and vegetables, but that's just for the family — not worth putting in the plan.
